Title: Self-service onboarding form bypasses approval recording
Description: 2 of 25 sampled new-hire accounts (nmiller2, bmoore) were created with no approver recorded, both through the self-service HRIS intake form rather than the manual IT request form.
Affected Scope: 2 of 25 sampled accounts; intake path affects any hire onboarded through the self-service form
Scoring Rationale: L3: one specific, still-active intake path produces this gap every time it is used. I3: breaks the audit trail for the approval step, but no evidence any inappropriate access actually resulted.

Title: HRIS sync delay produced a 13-day gap between hire and account creation
Description: One sampled account (dtorres) was not created until 13 calendar days after the documented hire date due to a start-date change not reflected in the HRIS sync batch.
Scoring Rationale: L2: tied to a specific start-date-change scenario, not a routine occurrence. I2: delays access rather than granting inappropriate access.

Title: IT Manager onboarding checklist grants standing Global Administrator by default
Description: The IT Manager onboarding checklist bundles tenant-wide Global Administrator access into standard onboarding, with no separate privileged-access request, approval, or change record. Confirmed on two accounts (wwright, mjackson2); change management testing (CR-01, CR-02) found no approval record for either grant.
Affected Scope: 2 confirmed accounts; systemic for any future IT Manager hire until the checklist is corrected
Scoring Rationale: L4: will recur for every future IT Manager hire under the current checklist. I4: standing tenant-wide admin granted with no review step at all.

Title: Legacy standing Global Administrator grant with no justification, review, or change record
Description: athompson (VP Engineering) holds standing Global Administrator dating to the company's early-stage period, before a formal change management process existed. No justification, no review since 2023, and no change record exists to retroactively approve.
Affected Scope: 1 confirmed account; unknown how many other pre-2023 grants may exist
Owner: CTO (spatel) and Director of IT & Security (psmith)
Scoring Rationale: L3: a known instance exists and the discovery method (sampling the current roster) would not reliably surface others like it. I4: standing tenant-wide admin held by someone whose current role does not require it.

Title: Standing admin account excluded from MFA enforcement by a change-management error
Description: A copy-paste error while updating the Conditional Access break-glass exclusion group (CR-10) added mjackson2, a standing Global Administrator, instead of the intended break-glass account. The error was never caught, leaving a real, named admin account fully excluded from MFA.
Scoring Rationale: L4: manual group-membership edits with no verification step are shown elsewhere in this audit (CM-01, 40% exception rate) to be unreliable. I5: a standing Global Administrator account with MFA completely bypassed is close to the most severe single-account exposure this audit can find.

Title: Break-glass account overdue for required test and rotation
Description: bg-admin2 has not been successfully tested or rotated since 2025-11-02, more than a year past the documented quarterly cadence.
Scoring Rationale: L3: lapses in a manual quarterly procedure with no automated reminder are plausible and already observed once. I4: an emergency-access credential that may not work, or that has sat unrotated and unmonitored for over a year, is a risk in both directions.

Title: Orphaned enabled accounts for terminated employees
Description: 2 of 25 terminated employees (wnelson, smiller) retain fully enabled accounts more than a year after termination, with no deprovisioning ticket found for either and no control currently in place to detect this after the fact.
Affected Scope: 2 of 25 terminated employees in the audit period
Owner: Director of People (jwalker) and Director of IT & Security (psmith)
Scoring Rationale: L4: has already occurred twice in a 25-person population with no detective control to catch a third. I4: a standing, unmonitored enabled credential for someone no longer employed.

Title: Account disablement can run significantly late with no explanation
Description: 1 of 25 terminated employees (nlee) had their account disabled 16 calendar days after termination, well outside the documented 3-business-day expectation, with no ticket explaining the delay.
Affected Scope: 1 of 25 terminated employees in the audit period
Owner: Director of People (jwalker) and Director of IT & Security (psmith)
Scoring Rationale: L3: the other 22 on-time cases show the process generally works, but nothing currently prevents or flags a late case like this one. I3: a 16-day window of continued access for a terminated employee, bounded but not trivial.

Title: MFA enrollment gap across 11 active accounts, including two management-tier accounts
Description: 11 of 210 active users (5.2%) are not enrolled in MFA despite Conditional Access policy CA01 requiring it tenant-wide with no documented exceptions. Two of the eleven are managers (Engineering Manager, Clinical Data Operations Manager).
Scoring Rationale: L4: the gap is already present across 6 of 13 departments, indicating an enrollment process issue rather than isolated oversights. I3: standard account impact for most of the 11, elevated for the 2 manager-tier accounts.

Title: Service account permits legacy authentication with no MFA-equivalent control
Description: svc-backup still permits legacy (basic) authentication, contradicting Conditional Access policy CA02, has no certificate- or managed-identity-based control in its place, and its password has not been rotated in over a year.
Affected Scope: 1 of 6 service accounts, holding Exchange and SharePoint Administrator roles
Scoring Rationale: L3: a known, standing configuration gap rather than an active incident. I4: legacy authentication is a well-documented bypass path for MFA, and this account holds administrative mail and file-storage roles.

Title: Sync service account holds Global Administrator, far broader than its function requires
Description: svc-hris-sync, which only needs to create and update user accounts, is assigned Global Administrator instead of the narrower User Administrator role, and its credential secret has never been rotated since the account was created in 2023.
Source: Incidental (found reviewing service-accounts.csv during MFA-02 and PAM testing; not in the original control matrix)
Scoring Rationale: L3: a standing configuration issue, not an active incident, but one that has persisted unexamined since 2023. I5: compromise of this specific account would be equivalent to a full tenant compromise, given the role it actually holds.

Title: CI/CD service principal scoped broader than its pipelines require
Description: svc-cicd holds subscription-level Contributor access and has not been reviewed since it was created, with no evidence its actual pipelines need that scope.
Source: Incidental (found reviewing service-accounts.csv during MFA-02 and PAM testing; not in the original control matrix)
Scoring Rationale: L2: no evidence of misuse, and the account uses a managed secrets vault rather than a clearly exposed credential. I3: broader-than-needed access is a real exposure but has not been shown to be actively exploited.

Title: Orphaned service account retains standing administrator rights after its supporting project closed
Description: svc-legacy-fileshare was created for a file-share migration project that closed out in early 2026, but the account remains enabled with standing SharePoint Administrator rights and no current business owner able to confirm it is still needed.
Source: Incidental (found reviewing service-accounts.csv during MFA-02 and PAM testing; not in the original control matrix)
Scoring Rationale: L3: parallels the orphaned human-account finding (F-07); nothing currently reviews service accounts after their supporting project ends. I3: standing admin rights with no current owner, but no evidence of misuse.

Title: Standard user access review coverage gap, including a department with no natural secondary reviewer
Description: 2 of 25 sampled active users (csanchez, ojackson) have no annual access review evidence on file. One of the two (ojackson) is the sole department head of a 5-person department, which has no obvious secondary approver to perform the review.
Scoring Rationale: L3: isolated gaps without a shared root cause across the sample, but one has a structural explanation (no natural reviewer) that would recur every cycle unless addressed. I2: a missed annual review is a control-evidence gap, not by itself an active exposure.

Title: Internal transfers do not consistently remove access tied to the prior role
Description: 2 of 10 sampled internal transfers (ksullivan, swatts) retain access from their previous department months to a year after the move. One case (swatts) involves retained access to the People department's HR records system, including personal data.
Owner: Director of IT & Security (psmith) and Director of People (jwalker)
Scoring Rationale: L4: 2 of a 10-item sample (20%) is a high rate for a control with no mechanism currently in place to remove prior-role access on a move. I4: the swatts case specifically involves retained access to personal data, a year after the employee left the department responsible for it.

Title: Manager-of-record not consistently updated after an internal transfer
Description: 1 of 10 sampled movers (bcollins) still shows their former manager in Entra ID three months after transferring departments, which also affects who is assigned to review their access under AR-02.
Scoring Rationale: L2: a single isolated case in the sample rather than a pattern. I2: an org-chart accuracy issue with a downstream effect on review assignment, not a direct access exposure on its own.

Title: Access-related changes are inconsistently governed by change management
Description: 4 of 10 sampled access-related changes (Conditional Access policy edits and privileged role assignments) lacked a complete, accurate, approved record. This gap is the traceable root cause of F-03, F-04, and F-05 above, not an independent issue.
Affected Scope: 4 of 10 sampled changes; root cause for 3 other findings in this log
Scoring Rationale: L4: a 40% exception rate in a 10-item sample, with at least one case (CR-10) showing the error was never caught after the fact. I5: this is the systemic finding; every other privileged-access finding in this audit that has a known cause traces back to a gap in this control.
